300. Bryan Adams was born in November 1959, meaning he was only nine years old in the summer of 1969—not old enough for the romance described in 'Summer of '69'.
299. Queen's 'Bohemian Rhapsody' has no chorus and was famously turned down as a single by several executives before becoming an all-time classic.
298. Dolly Parton wrote both 'I Will Always Love You' and 'Jolene' on the exact same night in 1973.
297. Eddie Van Halen played the melodic guitar solo on Michael Jackson's 'Beat It' as a favor and reportedly didn't charge a fee.
296. The Rolling Stones' '(I Can't Get No) Satisfaction' riff came to Keith Richards while he was asleep in a hotel room and recorded it onto a cassette recorder before falling back asleep.
295. Stevie Wonder was only 11 years old (billed as 'Little Stevie Wonder') when 'Fingertips' became a massive hit in 1963.
294. Creedence Clearwater Revival never had a #1 single on the Billboard Hot 100 despite releasing nine Top 10 hits.
293. Frank Sinatra's 'My Way' uses the melody of a French song called 'Comme d'habitude', with new English lyrics written by Paul Anka.
292. Fleetwood Mac's 'Rumours' was recorded while band members were breaking up with each other in real time.
291. Elton John and lyricist Bernie Taupin wrote 'Tiny Dancer' after a trip to California, long before it became a beloved slow-burn classic.
290. The Beach Boys' 'Good Vibrations' took months of studio sessions and dozens of tape splices rather than a single band take.
289. Bob Marley's 'No Woman, No Cry' actually means 'No woman, don't cry' in Jamaican patois.
288. Johnny Cash recorded 'Folsom Prison Blues' in the mid-1950s and later recorded a live album inside Folsom State Prison itself.
287. Blondie's 'Rapture' was one of the first songs featuring rap to hit #1 on the US Billboard Hot 100.
286. Journey's 'Don't Stop Believin'' had a quiet initial chart run in 1981 before exploding into a pop-culture staple decades later.
285. George Michael played almost all the instruments himself on the hit 'Faith'.
284. Heart's 'Barracuda' was written out of frustration over how music industry insiders were pitching and marketing the band.
283. Prince famously played 27 different instruments on his debut album 'For You'.
282. Cyndi Lauper's 'Time After Time' was co-written with Rob Hyman and inspired by the sci-fi film 'Mishima' / TV guide listings.
281. Tom Petty's 'Free Fallin'' came together rapidly after a spontaneous songwriting session with Jeff Lynne.
